body:
## Summary
- Add review synthesis recommended-next-step parsing and route `HUMAN_DECISION + SHIP` to `agent-self-approve` only when self-approval is enabled.
- Preserve non-`SHIP` `HUMAN_DECISION` as a stop and pass focused handoff context into self-approval.
- Update orchestrator workflow inputs, prompt guidance, docs, and focused regression tests.

## Verification
- `npm run build`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/handoff.test.js dist/__tests__/dispatch-agent-orchestrator-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #261

comments.body: @sepo-agent /answer I still don't get it -- it is still very complicated here. I am primary thinking about using a similar logic like how we handle `SHIP` -> when we detect SHIP then it will execute the certain next step. I think we can reuse a lot of logics there? However why we add some other infrastructures?

Yes, I think your mental model is right: this should reuse the existing `SHIP -> agent-self-approve` path, not create a separate orchestration concept.

The reason this PR has a little extra plumbing is that `SHIP` and `HUMAN_DECISION` come from two different review-synthesis fields:

- `SHIP` is the final verdict, already carried as `source_conclusion`.
- `HUMAN_DECISION` is the recommended next step, which previously was not carried through the handoff envelope.

So the minimal shape is:

1. Extract `Recommended Next Step` from the review synthesis.
   [handoff.ts#L213-L238](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L213-L238)

2. Pass it as `source_recommended_next_step` beside the existing `source_conclusion`.
   [dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L59-L84](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L59-L84)

3. In the same existing review handoff logic, special-case only:
   `sourceAction=review` + `sourceConclusion=SHIP` + `sourceRecommendedNextStep=HUMAN_DECISION` + self-approval enabled.
   [handoff.ts#L498-L523](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L498-L523)

4. Pass context into `agent-self-approve` so that agent knows what human decision was requested.
   [orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1552-L1557](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1552-L1557)

That is the “extra infrastructure”: not a new route, but carrying one extra structured field across the workflow boundary. Without that field, the orchestrator only sees `SHIP` and cannot tell whether the synthesis also said `HUMAN_DECISION`, nor can it give self-approval the focused context.

So the answer is: we are reusing the `SHIP` logic. The only addition I think is justified is the minimum plumbing needed to preserve `Recommended Next Step` and handoff context. We should not add broader `/orchestrate -> agent-self-approve` behavior for this case.

@sepo-agent /answer 

- OK but is there a really difference between source_conclusion vs sourceRecommendedNextStep ? 
- further more, in the current code, when we see HUMAN_DECISION, the orchestrator will also stop. Isn't it also a "source_conclusion"?

Yes, there is a real difference, but the naming makes it easy to blur.

`source_conclusion` means: **what did the previous action conclude?**

For a review synthesis, current deterministic code gets that from `## Final Verdict`:

- `SHIP`
- `MINOR_ISSUES`
- `NEEDS_REWORK`

That is what `extractReviewConclusion()` parses today:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L277-L284

`sourceRecommendedNextStep` means: **what does the synthesis recommend automation should do next?**

That comes from the separate `## Recommended Next Step` section:

- `FIX_PR`
- `HUMAN_DECISION`
- `NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`

The review synthesis prompt defines that separately from final verdict:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L105-L117

So this case can exist:

```md
## Recommended Next Step
HUMAN_DECISION: release timing needs maintainer judgment.

## Final Verdict
SHIP
```

If we collapse that into only `source_conclusion=HUMAN_DECISION`, we lose the important `SHIP` fact. That matters because `agent-self-approve` is only safe when there is a trusted current-head `SHIP` review synthesis.

If we keep only `source_conclusion=SHIP`, we lose the `HUMAN_DECISION` context and the self-approval agent will not know what judgment it is supposed to make.

So I would phrase it this way:

- `SHIP` is the **review result / safety gate**.
- `HUMAN_DECISION` is the **routing recommendation / context**.
- The self-approval path needs both.

On your second point: when the orchestrator “sees `HUMAN_DECISION` and stops,” that is currently prompt-level policy from the review synthesis recommendation, not a deterministic `source_conclusion`. The orchestrator prompt says to stop on `HUMAN_DECISION` unless self-approval is enabled for a `SHIP` review:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L76-L80

So no, I would not treat `HUMAN_DECISION` as another `source_conclusion`. It is better modeled as a second field, because it modifies what to do with the real conclusion.

The orchestrator prompt says to stop on HUMAN_DECISION unless self-approval is enabled for a SHIP review:

@sepo-agent /answer ok then given this, it seems currently orchestrator just reads the prompt and make the decisions? so even a simpler change is to just modify the prompt and tell the agent to launch self-approval when it sees HUMAN_DECISION + self-approval is allowed?

Prompt-only would be simpler, but it would only solve the **agent-planner path**, not the whole orchestrator behavior.

The orchestrator has two layers:

1. **Agent planner prompt**: can read context and propose a next action.
2. **Runtime handoff policy**: deterministic code that validates and dispatches the next workflow.

The prompt lives here:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L76-L80

But the deterministic review handoff lives here:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L459-L476

So if we only edit the prompt:

- It works only when the orchestrator planner actually runs in `agent` mode.
- It does not help `heuristics` mode.
- It requires the planner to rediscover/parse the latest review synthesis from GitHub, instead of using the review output already available at dispatch time.
- It still does not pass focused context into `agent-self-approve` unless we also change the workflow dispatch input.

So I’d avoid prompt-only as the core fix. The prompt should describe the rule, but the rule itself should be encoded in the runtime handoff policy.

Minimal robust fix is still:

- parse `Recommended Next Step`
- keep `source_conclusion=SHIP`
- carry `source_recommended_next_step=HUMAN_DECISION`
- let existing `SHIP -> agent-self-approve` handoff dispatch, with context
- keep non-`SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION` as stop

That keeps the agent prompt and deterministic runtime consistent.

> * keep non-`SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION` as stop

This is also weird. I think the whole point is to -- when there's HUMAN_DECISION, and regardless of whether it is ship or minor issues, we should then invoke the self-approval agent to check and recommend the next step.
@sepo-agent /answer you know what, maybe a even simpler solution is to remove HUMAN_DECISION from the review prompt output if self-approve and self-merge is enabled.

I would not do that as the main fix.

It sounds simpler, but it changes the meaning of the review synthesis output. `HUMAN_DECISION` is useful information: it means “the code may be technically okay, but there is a product/style/metadata/ambiguous judgment here.” That signal should not disappear just because self-approval/self-merge is enabled.

Two practical issues:

1. The review synthesis prompt currently does not receive `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE` or `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE`, so making its output conditional would require passing those settings into the review workflow anyway:
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L312-L331

2. If self-merge is enabled, hiding `HUMAN_DECISION` is actually riskier. The review might say `NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`/`SHIP`, then self-approval may approve, then self-merge may merge, while the original “this needs human judgment” signal was suppressed.

The better model is:

- Review synthesis should stay honest and emit `HUMAN_DECISION` when judgment is needed:
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L105-L117

- Self-approval should receive that context and decide:
  - `APPROVE` if the agent can safely make the call
  - `REQUEST_CHANGES` if there is concrete follow-up work
  - `BLOCKED` if it really should stay human

That matches the self-approval prompt’s existing contract:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-self-approve.md#L28-L31

So I’d keep `HUMAN_DECISION` in the review output. The minimal fix should route the narrow `SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION + self-approval enabled` case into `agent-self-approve` with the reason/context preserved, not erase the signal upstream.

@sepo-agent /answer ok fine then what are the concrete steps?

Concrete plan:

1. Keep review synthesis semantics unchanged.
   `## Recommended Next Step` stays separate from `## Final Verdict`:
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L105-L117

2. Add a small parser in `handoff.ts` for `Recommended Next Step`.
   Current code only extracts final verdict via `extractReviewConclusion()`:
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L277-L284

   Add:
   - `extractReviewRecommendedNextStep(markdown)`
   - `reviewNeedsHumanDecisionSelfApproval(markdown)`
   - `buildReviewSelfApprovalHandoffContext(markdown)`

3. Extend the handoff input with `sourceRecommendedNextStep`.
   This keeps `sourceConclusion=SHIP` while separately carrying `HUMAN_DECISION`.

4. Update review-originated handoff logic.
   Current `SHIP -> agent-self-approve` path already exists:
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L459-L476

   Add one branch before the normal `SHIP` branch:

   ```ts
   if recommendedNextStep === "human_decision":
     if conclusion === "ship" && allowSelfApprove:
       dispatch agent-self-approve with context
     else:
       stop for human decision
   ```

5. Update `dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts`.
   It already reads the review response and extracts `sourceConclusion`:
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L44-L52

   Add:
   - extract recommended next step from the same response file
   - pass `source_recommended_next_step`
   - build self-approval context only for `SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION`

6. Update `agent-orchestrator.yml`.
   Add a workflow input `source_recommended_next_step`, then pass it to:
   - planner env as `ORCHESTRATOR_SOURCE_RECOMMENDED_NEXT_STEP`
   - handoff CLI env as `SOURCE_RECOMMENDED_NEXT_STEP`

7. Update `orchestrate-handoff.ts`.
   Read `SOURCE_RECOMMENDED_NEXT_STEP`, pass it into `decideHandoff()`, and when dispatching `agent-self-approve`, forward `decision.handoffContext`.

8. Update `agent-self-approve.yml`.
   Add optional `source_handoff_context` input and feed it into the self-approval task as the request text/context, so the approval agent sees why the review said `HUMAN_DECISION`.

9. Update prompt/docs narrowly.
   In `agent-orchestrator.md`, say: if `sourceConclusion=SHIP`, `sourceRecommendedNextStep=HUMAN_DECISION`, and self-approval is enabled, hand off to `agent-self-approve`; otherwise `HUMAN_DECISION` stops.

10. Add focused tests.
   - `handoff.test.ts`: helper parsing, eligible dispatch, disabled stop, non-`SHIP` stop.
   - `dispatch-agent-orchestrator-cli.test.ts`: response with `HUMAN_DECISION + SHIP` dispatches orchestrator with both fields and context.
   - `orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.ts`: dispatches `agent-self-approve` with context only for eligible case.
   - envelope/docs tests if existing snapshots expect workflow inputs.

Verification:
- `npm run build`
- targeted node tests for handoff, dispatch, orchestrate
- `git diff --check`

@sepo-agent /answer 

1. what's implemented and not implemented in this PR? 
2. should we do a fix-pr or launch a new pr with implement?

For PR #262 specifically:

Implemented:

- Parses `Recommended Next Step` separately from `Final Verdict`.
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L213-L238

- Adds `sourceRecommendedNextStep` to handoff input and routes:
  `review + SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION + AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE=true -> agent-self-approve`.
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L498-L523

- Keeps non-`SHIP` `HUMAN_DECISION` as a stop.
  Same block: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L500-L511

- Extracts recommended next step in `dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts`, builds self-approval context, and passes `source_recommended_next_step`.
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L59-L84

- Adds `source_recommended_next_step` to `agent-orchestrator.yml` and passes it to both planner and deterministic handoff CLI.
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L12-L15

- Passes self-approval handoff context into `agent-self-approve.yml`.
  https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml#L15-L18

- Updates prompt/docs/tests for that narrow behavior.

Not implemented:

- It does **not** route `HUMAN_DECISION + MINOR_ISSUES` or `HUMAN_DECISION + NEEDS_REWORK` to `agent-self-approve`.
- It does **not** change self-approval’s trusted `SHIP` provenance requirement.
- It does **not** remove `HUMAN_DECISION` from review synthesis.
- It does **not** add broad manual `/orchestrate -> agent-self-approve` behavior.

For the second question: if the desired behavior is still the narrow `SHIP + HUMAN_DECISION` route, I would not launch a new PR. PR #262 already implements it.

If you want to change the behavior to “any `HUMAN_DECISION`, regardless of final verdict, should invoke `agent-self-approve` to recommend approve/request-changes/block,” then use **fix-pr on this PR**, not a new implement PR. This PR already owns the touched code paths, so a new PR would likely duplicate/conflict. But that is a scope change: we would also need to decide whether self-approval is still allowed to require `SHIP`, or whether it becomes more of a “decision gate” for non-`SHIP` reviews.

Yes. If the requirement is now:

> whenever review synthesis says `HUMAN_DECISION`, activate the self-approval agent

then PR #262 is **not quite right**.

What PR #262 currently does is narrower:

```ts
if recommendedNextStep === "human_decision":
  if conclusion === "ship" && allowSelfApprove:
    dispatch agent-self-approve
  else:
    stop
```

That means `HUMAN_DECISION + MINOR_ISSUES` and `HUMAN_DECISION + NEEDS_REWORK` still stop:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9e117997c317d895597388d3ebf5e292cfcf5c0c/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L500-L511

There is also a second issue: even if we dispatch `agent-self-approve` for non-`SHIP`, the current self-approval preflight requires the latest trusted synthesis verdict to be `SHIP`:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/self-approval.ts#L188-L195

So just changing the handoff branch is not enough. The self-approval workflow would likely stop before the agent runs for `MINOR_ISSUES` / `NEEDS_REWORK`.

The cleaner fix would be:

- Route **any** `review + HUMAN_DECISION + AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE=true` to `agent-self-approve`.
- Pass the review verdict and human-decision context into self-approval.
- Let `agent-self-approve` run as a decision gate.
- Keep the safety rule: it may only submit an actual GitHub approval when trusted current-head verdict is `SHIP`.
- For non-`SHIP`, it should return `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `BLOCKED`, not approve.

So yes, this should be a **fix-pr on PR #262**, not a new implementation PR. The PR already owns the relevant files; the fix is to broaden the `HUMAN_DECISION` dispatch behavior and adjust self-approval preflight/prompt/tests so non-`SHIP` cases can run the agent but cannot accidentally approve.
